question: How is a quality value in a content negotiation header field interpreted?

claims.text: A quality value in the content negotiation fields is the value of the case-insensitive "q" parameter, which assigns a relative weight to the preference for the associated kind of content.
A quality value is normalized to a real number from 0 through 1, with 0.001 as the least preferred value and 1 as the most preferred value.
A quality value of 0 means that the associated kind of content is not acceptable.
If no "q" parameter is present, the default quality value is 1.
A sender of a quality value must not generate more than three digits after the decimal point.
